subject: Multi-region SI pilot: segmented data residency & integration checklist
messages:
From: Martin Dupont <partnerships@innotech.eu>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: camila_reyes@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 05 Feb 2026 08:31:00 +0000
Subject: Proposal: joint SI pilot across EU & APAC (initial ask)

Hi Jonas / Camila,

Thanks again for carving out time yesterday. As discussed, Innotech is keen to run a joint pilot that showcases Redwood's serving runtime integrated by two local SIs: one for the EU (Sven/DE) and one for Japan (Hikari). The two asks from our side:

- Can Redwood support a segmented data residency model where EU customer data remains in EU zones while APAC piloted customers route to a Japan footprint?
- What are the integration touchpoints your team expects (SAML, KMS access, audit log export, and model variant routing)?

Attached is a short pilot brief with scope and success metrics (pilot length, throughput targets, sample workload). We have a tentative customer in Tokyo and a proof-of-concept customer in Munich.

Key timelines: we are hoping to run the pilot in March if we can get a technical checklist and compliance evidence by mid-February. Any gaps on your side?

Thanks,
Martin Dupont
Partnerships, Innotech Solutions
[Attachment: partner-pilot-brief.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Martin Dupont <partnerships@innotech.eu>
Cc: camila_reyes@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 05 Feb 2026 11:08:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Proposal: joint SI pilot across EU & APAC (initial ask)

Hi Martin — great to hear and thanks for the brief. Short answers up front: yes, we can support segmented residency with a per-tenant routing policy and distinct store locations for KV/prefix caches. The implementation details differ slightly between our Hosted (regional clusters) and Dedicated (customer-dedicated pools) offerings, which will affect latency and cost.

I've attached our SI onboarding checklist to capture the technical inputs we need from each SI (network, SAML metadata, supported quantization profile, model size, expected peak RPS). Can you confirm that Sven (DE) and Hikari's integration lead will fill these?

I'm looping Grace (partner ops) to outline integration patterns and Stephanie (security lead) to confirm required compliance artifacts (SOC2 report, encryption-in-transit details, and evidence for key management).

Proposed next steps:
- Hikari + Sven to fill the checklist by 2026-02-13
- Redwood to provide SOC2 and sample audit log export by 2026-02-12
- Align on pilot success metrics and SLA for Japan region by 2026-02-16

Attachments: SI_Onboarding_Checklist.xlsx

Best,
Jonas Weber

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com

Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 06 Feb 2026 09:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Proposal: joint SI pilot across EU & APAC (initial ask)

Thanks all — I sketched out two integration patterns in the attached note:

1) Segmented-residency (preferred): per-tenant routing with region-scoped object stores and KV caches. Minimal data egress between zones; requires SI to host a light-weight connector (nginx proxy + auth) in each region.

2) Centralized-controlplane / regional-runtime: control plane in EU, runtime nodes in each region. Simpler for rollouts but adds cross-border audit-log streaming.

For the pilot I recommend Pattern 1 because it isolates customer data while allowing us to test routing policies. I've listed practical checkboxes in the doc (network CIDRs, SAML issuer URLs, cert rotation cadence).

Attaching integration-patterns.md — please review and flag any redlines.

Grace O'Connor
Partner Operations
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: integration-patterns.md (text/markdown)]

Hi Jonas / team,

Thanks for the checklist and patterns. A few technical points from Hikari's side:

- Latency: our customer SLAs are sensitive to p99 token latency — can you confirm expected p99 in Tokyo for a ~2k token prompt on Dedicated nodes?
- KV / cache: will regional KV caches be consistent across zones or eventually consistent? We need to know for session continuity.
- Compliance: our legal lead requests a copy of Redwood's SOC2 (or equivalent) plus a data-flow diagram that shows where logs and model outputs land.

I've attached Hikari's technical requirements doc for the pilot. We'll get the checklist back by 2026-02-12.

Regards,
Takeo Sato
